solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Forecast operating cost must change

indicators.note: letters that must change are compelled into a different order

parts.note: both words taken as written, thirteen letters in all

explanation.surface: A budget prediction: running costs are going to have to rise or fall.
explanation.definitionFit: To prognosticate is to predict the future, a formal synonym of the verb forecast.

clue.text: He makes good stuff

parts.note: surface reading: a craftsman who produces quality goods
setter's reading: to make good is to mend, so this is someone who fixes broken things

explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes good stuff' reads as producing fine work; the trick is the phrase 'make good', meaning restore or put right.
explanation.definitionFit: A tradesman who mends broken appliances and fittings restores them, which is what making good means.

clue.text: Starts action on both sides in order to leave Europeans

indicators.note: the chosen letters depart from the longer word, so they are struck out of it

parts.note: people from Germany are Europeans

indicators.note: only the letters standing at either edge of the word are wanted

parts.note: the first and last letters of action

explanation.surface: Instructions for a manoeuvre: get things moving on the flanks so that the Europeans withdraw.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking AN out of GERMANS leaves GERMS. 'Starts' looks like a verb but is a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A germ is a beginning or seed from which something develops, as in the germ of an idea.

clue.text: Char in charge of chef

parts.note: someone over a team is in charge of it
a chef is a cook

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady (a char) put in charge of the kitchen's chef.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English a char is also a charwoman, a cleaner, which is how the surface reads it; here it is the verb meaning scorch.
explanation.definitionFit: To char food is to burn it by cooking too long, which is to overcook it.

clue.text: Put bits of bread at front of tunnel for cave-dwellers

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: first letter of tunnel
bread rolls are small portions of bread

explanation.surface: Leaving a trail of breadcrumbs at a tunnel entrance to lure something out of a cave.
explanation.walkthrough: The rolls are placed after the front of the tunnel, so T comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scandinavian folklore trolls are ugly creatures living in caves or under bridges.

clue.text: It's painful to see Bill struggling in manacle

indicators.note: someone struggling twists about, so the letters of the name are jumbled
one part is placed inside the restraint word

parts.note: a manacle is a chain for the wrists
the name rearranged

explanation.surface: A sad sight: a prisoner named Bill struggling in his shackles.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the whole phrase 'It's painful': the answer is a thing that hurts.
explanation.definitionFit: A chilblain is a sore, itchy swelling on fingers or toes caused by cold, a notoriously painful complaint.

clue.text: Volunteer force takes politician over a US resort.

parts.note: the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force
Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A militia carries a politician off to an American holiday town.
explanation.walkthrough: TA (Territorial Army) is the standard crossword volunteer force.
explanation.definitionFit: Tampa is a Florida city on the Gulf coast, popular with holidaymakers, so a resort in the US.

clue.text: Foundation altering NHS timetables

indicators.note: altering something changes its make-up, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A charitable trust is reorganising the schedules of Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.walkthrough: The NHS is the UK's state health service, which fits a charitable foundation meddling with it.
explanation.definitionFit: An establishment is an institution set up for a purpose, as a foundation is; both also mean the act of founding.

clue.text: Marshal pens directive for senior politician

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or organise, so the letters are set in new order

parts.note: both words taken as written

explanation.surface: A military marshal drafts an order intended for a high-ranking official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' reads as a noun, an officer writing orders, but works as the verb meaning arrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice president is second only to the president, such as the US number two, so a top-ranking politician.

clue.text: Fictional character wandering around Peru with horse

indicators.note: roaming about aimlessly suggests letters that move out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A storybook hero roams the Andes of Peru on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: A superhero such as Superman is an invented figure with extraordinary powers from comics and films.

clue.text: I deface cute deer's feet

indicators.note: to take the face off something is to remove its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
Bambi is the Disney fawn

explanation.surface: A vandal confesses to spoiling the hooves of an adorable deer.
explanation.walkthrough: BAMBI loses its first letter, B, and follows I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iambi is the plural of iambus, a metrical foot of one short and one long syllable, so feet in verse.

clue.text: American schoolgirl's out of order

parts.note: A is a standard abbreviation for American
a miss is a young girl

explanation.surface: A US schoolgirl has misbehaved and is being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is wrong or not as it should be, which is what out of order means.

clue.text: Observe famous person in front of judge

parts.note: short for celebrity
to rate is to assess or judge

explanation.surface: Watch a celebrity standing before the judge in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe a festival or anniversary is to mark it with ceremony, which is to celebrate it.

clue.text: Being cut left a doctor and policeman outside hospital

indicators.note: one piece stands around another, enclosing it

parts.note: standard abbreviation for left
taken as written
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
slang for a police officer
H is the map abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: An injured person abandoned by a doctor and a constable outside the hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: COP wraps round H. The definition is read as a cut taken from a being, a young sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamb chop is a cut of meat from a lamb, so it is a portion cut from a living creature.

clue.text: Enjoy the present from Rome!

parts.note: surface reading: delight in a gift sent from Italy
setter's reading: the present moment, and the advice to make the most of it, in Latin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Present' looks like a gift; it is the present time, and 'from Rome' signals the phrase is Latin, from Horace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin motto means seize the day: live for today rather than worrying about the future.

clue.text: Butcher's male goose

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rhyming slang, butcher's hook for look, so a quick look

explanation.walkthrough: In Cockney rhyming slang 'have a butcher's' (butcher's hook = look) means take a look; a gander is a look in British slang too.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a glance or look in British slang and the male of the goose.

clue.text: Push aside pan and fish in wine

parts.note: to pan or dis is to criticise harshly

indicators.note: one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: red wine
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Cooking instructions: shove aside the pan and poach fish in wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like a cooking pan but is the slang verb for slating a play or film, as is DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To disregard something is to ignore it, to set it aside as unimportant.

clue.text: Course it's very controversial if I join environmentalists — mostly green

indicators.note: the single letter joins the group by going in among its members

parts.note: Friends of the Earth, the environmental group
taken as written

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a green is an area of grass

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether joining the eco-campaigners would make them notorious.
explanation.walkthrough: FOE stands for Friends of the Earth. The definition is a course of a meal, controversial because the birds are force-fed.
explanation.definitionFit: Foie gras, fattened goose or duck liver, is served as a starter course and divides opinion over force-feeding.

clue.text: Dispatched message to railway guard

parts.note: a message is sent when it is dispatched
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A telegram has been sent off to the railway company.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry is a soldier posted to keep watch, a guard at a gate or post.

clue.text: Urgent request for help follows commando finally joining desert rats

indicators.note: the letter joins in, slipping into the middle of the next word

parts.note: a desert is a stretch of sand

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is used

parts.note: last letter of commando
the distress signal

explanation.surface: A distress call from a commando unit fighting alongside the Desert Rats in North Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The Desert Rats were Britain's 7th Armoured Division in the Second World War, so 'desert rats' looks like one phrase; it splits, with 'rats' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: So-and-sos are unpleasant people, a mild word for rotters, just as rats are.

clue.text: Old priest's extremely forgetful — so be it

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters

parts.note: first and last letters of forgetful
amen means so be it, said at the end of a prayer

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric is very absent-minded, and he accepts it with a shrug.
explanation.definitionFit: A flamen was a priest of a particular god in ancient Rome, so an old priest.

clue.text: One interrupts vendor shortly after stain is seen on fabric

indicators.note: breaking into the middle of a word puts the letter inside it
cut short, the word loses its last letter
this word places the trading part behind the blemish part

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or blemish
a vendor is a seller
Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shop assistant spots a mark on the cloth and breaks off a sale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabric' looks like the setting rather than the definition; the answer is a cloth named after the French port, not the city itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Marseille, or marcella, is a stiff cotton fabric with a raised woven pattern, used for bedspreads.

clue.text: Port and nearly a carafe of wine

indicators.note: nearly the whole of something means it is a letter short at the end

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port
a carafe is a jar

explanation.surface: An order at the bar: some port and nearly a whole carafe of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'carafe' gives a jar; 'a' is read as a link here, and JAR loses its final R. 'Port' looks like the fortified wine but is a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red or white Spanish wine from the La Rioja region.

clue.text: Request van after parking

indicators.note: this word puts the vanguard piece second, behind the parking abbreviation

parts.note: P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking
the van, short for vanguard, is the lead position

explanation.surface: Asking for a delivery van once it has been parked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Van' looks like a vehicle; it is the vanguard, the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to beg or make an earnest appeal, so to request.

clue.text: Where you might find scavengers looking over bread

indicators.note: looking back over something runs your eye the other way along it

parts.note: scavengers rummage at the tip, a British word for rubbish dump

explanation.surface: Rubbish-dump scavengers look over a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: A tip is a British rubbish dump; read the phrase AT TIP backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitta is a flat, slightly leavened bread from the Middle East and Mediterranean.

clue.text: I grumble about biblical woman

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: taken as written
to moan is to grumble

explanation.surface: Someone complains about a woman from the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is Ruth's mother-in-law in the Old Testament Book of Ruth.

clue.text: Couple after book — by him?

indicators.note: this word sends the pair piece behind the scripture piece

parts.note: the Gospel of Mark, a book of the Bible
twain is an old word for two, a couple

explanation.surface: A pair hunting for a book written by a particular author.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also hints at the writer: a book could be by him, and the question mark flags the double reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark Twain, the pen name of Samuel Clemens, wrote Huckleberry Finn, so a book may well be by him.

clue.text: Letter read out to staff is about final plans to acquire colony

indicators.note: reading something out says it, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: the name of the letter K, spelt as the word for a low island
to staff a post is to man it
taken as written
to land a deal or job is to acquire it

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is the one taken

parts.note: last letter of plans

explanation.surface: A dictated letter tells staff about final arrangements for taking over a territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does no work beyond joining the pieces. The Caymans are a British Overseas Territory in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cayman Islands remain a British Overseas Territory, formerly called a colony, governed from London.
